Fehu: The candle kept for a special evening has never been lit.
The battery you never use is flat on the day you need it.
The pool cut off from the river clouds over while the river runs clear.
The bucket under the spring is full, and the water goes on running over its brim.
After weeks on the sofa, the stiff knee meets the stairs.
The breath has to go out before the next one can come in.
Uruz: The lid holds, and holds, and then turns in your hand.
The salmon throws itself at the falls again.
The door swollen by rain opens at the third push of your shoulder.
Thurisaz: The reply is written in a single breath, and your thumb stops above the send button.
The cold of the river at your ankles stops you before the current does.
Your foot is already off the kerb when the horn sounds.
The answer is already on your tongue, and you take one long breath before it.
Ansuz: One person says the name no one has said all evening, and the table goes quiet.
Said aloud, the plan sounds different from the one in your head.
The raven calls once from the roof, and everyone at the door looks up.
Raidho: The path across the grass is on no plan; it is where everyone actually walks.
On the long drive you miss your turning because the road was so easy to follow.
After the first hour of walking your feet stop asking how far it is.
Kenaz: The phone light finds the dropped key, and beside it a long-lost earring.
The new bulb in the hallway shows a crack that was always in the ceiling.
One match in the cave shows the wall an arm's length away and no further.
Gebo: You bring a dish to the shared dinner and leave with a plate of someone else's cooking.
The borrowed book comes back with a bar of chocolate on top.
Someone has remembered how you take your coffee.
The rowan feeds the thrush, and the thrush carries its seed over the hill.
A gift you did not ask for sits on your table, still in its paper.
The plank across the stream holds because each bank carries one end.
Wunjo: Halfway through the dishes a song comes on, and you both join in.
Dinner is burnt, and the table laughs over bread and cheese.
On the first warm day the doors along the street stand open.
Hagalaz: The flight is cancelled at the gate, and the queue turns round as one.
A power cut ends the video call and takes the unsaved slide with it.
One minute of hail, and the tulips are lying on the path.
Nauthiz: The phone is at two per cent, and you send the one message that matters.
One seat is left on the last bus, and two of you are still on the pavement.
The birch on the lava field grows along the one crack that holds soil.
Isa: The waterfall has become a wall of ice, its last streams held against the rock.
A chain of bubbles rises through the dark water, then stops beneath the clear ice.
A drop has frozen at the tip of an icicle, just before it falls.
The lift stops between floors, and the building goes on humming around it.
Jera: The tree planted as a sapling beside the bench now shades the place where you sit.
After months of practice, you answer in the new language without translating first.
The coins dropped in the jar each evening are, one day, the fare.
Eihwaz: The footbridge sways under the crowd and is still again when they have crossed.
The tall grass lies flat in the wind and is standing again by evening.
The runner slows to a walk on the hill and does not stop.
Perth: A parcel sits on the step, taped shut, with no sender's name.
An unnamed voice memo sits in your phone, three minutes long.
The whale has dived, and everyone on the boat watches a different patch of water.
You write down the teacher's words, not yet knowing what they are for.
Algiz: The door opens on its chain, just far enough to see who is knocking.
The phone is silenced for the night, with three numbers allowed to ring through.
The flock feeds head down, and one goose stands with its neck straight.
Sowilo: The cloud lifts, and you see how far up the slope you already are.
The low sun comes in under the cloud, and the stones on the moor have shadows.
The sun comes round to the window, and every fingerprint on the glass shows.
Tiwaz: Everyone agreed in the corridor; on the form there is one name, and it is yours.
You tell the referee the ball was out, and your own team loses the point.
You turn down the praise and say whose work it was.
Berkana: The child struggles with the zip, and you wait while they try again.
The seedling droops for a week in its new pot, then puts out one leaf.
The eider plucks her own down to line the nest.
Ehwaz: Two people walk side by side, and neither could say who set the pace.
Two people carry a long mirror through the doorway, one pausing as the other turns.
Two swans cross the lake, and the gap between them stays the same.
Mannaz: You hear your own phrase come out of a friend's mouth and learn how it sounds.
A friend copies the way you tap your foot, and you had never noticed it.
In the dark window of the train your own face sits among the other passengers.
Laguz: Your foot finds the brake as the car ahead drifts, before you know why.
You turn back at the door, sure something is left behind, before you know what.
The swell lifts the boat before any wave can be seen.
Ingwaz: The dough rests under a tea towel, and by morning it has doubled.
The broken bone knits under the cast, and nothing can be seen of it.
The potato forgotten in the cupboard has put out white shoots.
Othila: The recipe card is in another hand, with one change added in yours.
The table has moved through three homes and still stands in the kitchen.
The stream runs in the bed the old river cut.
Dagaz: You read the same message again in the morning, and it says something else.
You turn the map on your phone, and the street falls into place.
The tide has turned, and the same boats now point the other way.
Blank: A new document is open, and the cursor blinks on the first line.
One wall in the new flat is still bare, without a single nail hole.
Fresh snow lies on the field, and nothing has crossed it yet.
